### **The BC Climate Anomaly App**

#### **Background**

This application is designed to visualize and provide data on **monthly**, **seasonal**, and **annual** climate normals, anomalies and trends across, western north America, BC and BC's sub regions ( eco-regions, watersheds, municipalities etc.) over the period of 1950 to present. It offers spatial visualizations, interactive plots, and reports on historical climate changes. Key climate parameters include:

- Precipitation
- Temperature (minimum, maximum, and mean)
- Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD)
- Relative Humidity (RH)
- Soil Moisture( 0 - 1m)

The app displays anomalies in comparison to long-term average climate conditions across **Western North America**, **British Columbia (BC)**, and BC's sub-regions (**eco-provinces**,**eco-regions**, **eco-sections**, **Municipalities**, **major watersheds**, <a href='https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/data/geographic-data-services/topographic-data/freshwater' target='_blank'>**Freshwater Atlas (FWA) watersheds**</a>, and <a href='https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/industry/forestry/managing-our-forest-resources/forest-landscape-plans' target='_blank'>**Forest Landscape Plan (FLP) boundaries**</a>).

Additionally, the app provides insights into the **magnitude and statistical significance of trends** for spatially averaged anomalies for selected regions and parameters. Users have the flexibility to select any of these climate parameters to observe spatial and temporal changes within their chosen region for specific month, season or year. The apps outputs include:

- Anomaly time-series plot and trends
- Spatial anomaly maps with summary
- Climate normals maps with summary
- Spatial trends map and summaries for 1950 - present and  1980 - present

#### **Anomaly App Page**

The **Anomaly App** page as a main application interface, offers:

- Anomaly time-series plot and trends
- Spatial anomaly maps with summary
- Climate normals maps with summary
- Spatial trends map and summaries for 1950 - present and  1980 - present

Users have options to save the maps and plots generated by the application, obtain the full report in HTML format, and download associated data.

#### **Download Data and Plots**

- **Download Plot**: Saves plots in `.PNG` format, including region, parameter, and and start and end years (or years of climate normal) in the filename.
- **Download Anomaly Time Series Data**: Downloads spatially averaged time series data as `.csv`, including columns for year (`yr`), anomaly value (`ano`), parameter (`par`), month (`Mon`), and region. 
- **Download Raster Data**: Downloads spatial anomaly and climate normal data in `.GTiff` format, with each band containing data for one year..

**Units**

- Temperature (`tmean`, `tmax`, `tmin`): °C
- Precipitation and Soil Moisture: % of normal
- VPD: Pa
- RH: %

Note: Anomaly data is land-only. If the selected region does not overlap landmass, the app will return an error — reset the app to continue.

**Report** page provides a link to an HTML reports that include monthly summary ( upto recent month) reports, annual summary (2024 onwards) reports and  a general overview report spanning from 1980 to 2022. 

#### **Data and Methods**

This tool and its reports help users understand how climate parameters have changed from long term average at monthly, seasonal and annual level in BC and sub-regions. The app uses <a href='https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/cdsapp#!/dataset/reanalysis-era5-land?tab=overview' target='_blank'>ERA5-Land hourly data</a> from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). The ERA5-Land is a gridded reanalysis dataset combining observational and model data at ~9 km spatial and hourly temporal resolution.

**Anomalies** are computed relative to **1981–2010 climatological normals**. 
For temperature, VPD, and RH, the anomaly is computed as:

$$
\text{par}_{ano} = x - \bar{x}
$$

while for precipitation and soil moisture the anomaly is computed as:

$$
\text{par}_{ano} = \frac{x - \bar{x}}{\bar{x}}
$$

where $x$ is the observed value and $\bar{x}$ is the climate normal.

The anomalies data are regridded to spatial resolution of about 30 km by 30 km.
We used **Mann-Kendall Test** to assess the significance of linear and spatial trends while the **Theil-Sen Estimator** is used to calculate trend magnitudes for the period of 1950–present and 1980-present.
